tier_reason: The repo README has only absolute exectime/utilization sample output, with no Cilk or OpenMP comparison. The PLDI 2018 paper (chargueraud.org, irif.fr, HAL) is EGRESS_BLOCKED, and WebSearch snippets say only that heartbeat 'generally matched or beat' the Cilk Plus PBBS programs on 40 cores, with overheads under 5% versus over 25%. No per-benchmark number could be confirmed, so the B rests on an unopened paper and is capped at C until someone reads it.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (paper not opened): on ten PBBS benchmarks, the heartbeat prototype generally matched or beat the Cilk Plus PBBS implementations on 40 cores; task-creation overheads stayed under 5% versus sometimes over 25% for PBBS granularity control. The record's '16-queens 1.86x on a dual dual-core machine' could not be traced to this paper.
corrections.caveats: No license file (LICENSE, LICENSE.txt, LICENSE.md and COPYING all 404), so reference only. Paper PDF EGRESS_BLOCKED; numbers come from search snippets. The '16-queens 1.86x' figure in the original record is unverified and may come from a different paper. The README shows no comparison with Cilk, OpenMP or TBB. Research prototype with interpretive overheads; Cilk Plus is obsolete. Last commit 2022-07-01.

notes: Real peer-reviewed work (PLDI 2018) and a candidate to go back to B if a retier can open the paper (try a raw.githubusercontent copy). The record's specific number looks misattributed.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed IPDPS 2021 paper (cited in the README) compares Nowa against lock-based Cilk Plus and TBB and against OpenMP tasks (libomp). WebSearch snippets match the record exactly: up to 1.64x and 1.17x on average at 256 hardware threads, and 8.68x on average over OpenMP. The paper PDF (www4.cs.fau.de) is EGRESS_BLOCKED, so the numbers come from snippets.

corrections.caveats: Paper (IEEE IPDPS 2021, www4.cs.fau.de PDF) and Zenodo are EGRESS_BLOCKED; numbers come from WebSearch snippets. The mirror repo has a benchmark directory and run_benchmarks.sh but no numbers in its README. Based on Fibril (chaoran/fibril); the LICENSE is MIT (Chaoran Yang 2014, Pfeiffer and Schmaus 2020). The GitHub mirror has 0 stars; the original artifact is Zenodo record 4541475. Last commit 2022-10-01. Cilk Plus is obsolete.

notes: The MIT license was confirmed from the LICENSE file. A retier could reach A if the paper states compiler, flags and CPU, since the benchmark code is public.

tier_reason: First-party Google Benchmark results in the README against Taskflow (Taskflow's own fibonacci, linear_chain and matrix_multiplication examples at commit 9616467). Hardware is stated but compiler and flags are not, and the arXiv 2407.15805 preprint is by the same author and not peer-reviewed, so the record is C, not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README Google Benchmark wall times: Fibonacci n=35 1,661 ms vs Taskflow 15,058 ms (~9x, derived from page data); linear chain of 33,554,432 tasks 4,158 ms vs 9,951 ms (~2.4x, derived from page data); matrix multiplication is slower than Taskflow at every size (2048: 4,134 ms vs 3,970 ms; 256: 8.20 ms vs 4.13 ms).
corrections.hardware: Stated as 'Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU i7-1165G7 @ 2.80GHz with 32 CPUs', Debian GNU/Linux 12 (that CPU name and count are inconsistent: the i7-1165G7 has 8 threads)
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers; compiler and flags not stated; single-iteration runs for the large sizes. Matrix multiplication is slower than Taskflow at all sizes. The hardware string is self-contradictory (i7-1165G7 reported as Xeon with 32 CPUs). The arXiv preprint (2407.15805, blocked here) is not peer-reviewed. Baseline is Taskflow, not oneTBB. The large Fibonacci gap may reflect Taskflow's subflow overhead for recursive tasks.

notes: MIT OR Apache-2.0, 67 stars and last commit 2024-11-29 were confirmed from the repo pages.
